queries.query: "large language model" OR LLM "network configuration" generation intent-to-configuration "network automation"
queries.rationale: Locate direct prior work translating natural-language intent to device configurations or automation scripts using LLMs; establishes immediate phenomenon and comparable experimental tasks.
Find studies or toolchains that pair generation with validators/repair loops (e.g., Batfish) for network configs to inform mitigation architectures.
Survey a principal practical verifier used in NetOps research to understand available validators and their expressible properties and limits.

queries.query: "Header Space Analysis" HSA "network verification" NetPlumber "network verification"
queries.rationale: Capture foundational formal/algorithmic verification mechanisms (HSA, NetPlumber) that define correctness criteria and simulator fidelity for evaluation.

queries.query: "intent-based networking" "intent to configuration" automated intent translation
queries.rationale: Map prior intent-based networking research to current LLM approaches; identify differences in specification, ambiguity handling, and verification.
Locate AIOps/NetOps benchmark efforts and assessments of LLMs for operational tasks to judge benchmark validity and gaps.
Search for reported LLM hallucination incidents specific to network automation (fabricated commands, unsupported features) to characterize operational failure modes.
source_preferences: GitHub issue threads with reproducible traces

queries.query: "tool-augmented LLM" OR "agentic" "network operations" ReAct "Toolformer" LangChain AutoGPT
queries.rationale: Identify agentic/Tool-augmented architectures (ReAct, Toolformer, LangChain-style pipelines) applied to or adaptable for NetOps orchestration and risks introduced by agentic behavior.
Find literature on verifier-in-the-loop or iterative self-correction techniques (generate–validate–repair) applicable to configuration safety and bounded correction.
Survey formal verification approaches leveraging SMT/constraint solvers for policy compliance and their suitability as validators in LLM-driven pipelines.
Identify simulation/testbed environments for executing and validating generated configs; assess realism vs. production and integration feasibility into evaluation loops.
Locate existing benchmark suites for NetOps/AIOps to assess task realism, dataset construction, and gaps relevant to LLM evaluation.

queries.query: "evaluation metrics" "configuration correctness" reachability isolation loop-freedom "policy compliance"
queries.rationale: Collect definitions and measurement practices for correctness metrics used in network verification and operational validation.
Find cross-disciplinary work on safety/trust metrics for autonomous operational agents to frame mitigation, disclosure, and human-in-the-loop requirements.
Search for practical case studies where LLMs generated vendor-specific device commands or automation playbooks to discover common error classes and validation needs.
Identify work on adversarial or robustness testing of configuration systems and LLMs to inform threat models and perturbation-based evaluation protocols.
Survey operational practices for manual validation, runbook-based checks, and escalation to compare against autonomous workflows and design hybrid mitigations.
Gather methodological best practices for reproducible LLM experiments (prompt/seed reporting, temperature, model versions) to inform preregistration and artifact recording.
Find comparative and survey papers on network verification tools to establish nearest-neighbor methods and baselines for validator selection and limits.
Locate public datasets of device configurations and network topologies suitable for building tasks, training evaluators, or reproducing experiments.

inclusion_criteria: Peer-reviewed conference/journal publications and ACM/IEEE proceedings
ArXiv and preprints when primary source is clear and code/data are available
Public tool documentation and GitHub repositories containing verifiable code/artifacts (e.g., Batfish, Mininet)
Public benchmarks, datasets, and testbeds with accessible descriptions and artifacts
IETF RFCs or working-group drafts directly relevant to configuration syntax/semantics
Technical reports and reproducible industry case studies with sufficient methodological detail
Publicly accessible evaluation artifacts (scripts, prompts, seeds) enabling replication
English-language sources or translated authoritative documents
exclusion_criteria: Non-technical marketing materials or vendor promotional content without technical substantiation
Social-media posts, unreferenced blog claims, or forum threads lacking verifiable artifacts (unless they link to reproducible evidence)
Proprietary internal reports or datasets inaccessible to outside researchers
Works that only evaluate generic language understanding unrelated to NetOps tasks (unless they include operational artifacts)
Sources that cannot be verified by DOI/arXiv/official project pages or archived snapshots
date_rationale: Cover seminal verification and NetOps methods historically (pre-2016) but emphasize literature from 2018–2026, with special focus on 2020–2026 because LLM and agentic tool-augmentation advances accelerated during this period; include older foundational verification work (HSA, NetPlumber, Batfish introductions) to ground validators.
